paper.title: Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing
paper.central_claim: Treating a group of agents as the evolutionary unit - selecting a parent group by a performance-novelty score and letting every member reflect on the pooled evolutionary traces of the group - consolidates exploratory diversity better than tree-structured evolution (DGM), reaching 71.0% on SWE-bench Verified and 88.3% on Polyglot, matching or exceeding human-designed frameworks, transferring across coding models and repairing injected framework bugs faster.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

sections_read: Opus: pinned text read before opening seat records (abstract, method, experiments, all tables, appendices; long proof derivations skimmed) ; targeted re-reads for every disputed field

evidence.quote: In fact, AI agents can directly share trajectories, tools, and learned artifacts, and they can aggregate complementary skills without the constraints of reproduction or lineage.
evidence.support_explanation: 被审核的单亲隔离假设及可行替代，不是生物隐喻本身。

evidence.quote: We represent each agent
evidence.support_explanation: 二进制任务成功向量刻画行为；后接KNN余弦新颖性与性能乘积。

evidence.quote: The aggregated traces from all agents in the parent group are provided as shared input to every agent. Each agent evolves from this shared pool of group-level experience while diverging through complementary adaptations to its own codebase, enabling the group to explore diverse evolutionary directions while leveraging experiences from one another.
evidence.support_explanation: 共享失败轨迹/框架patch条件化反思和重写，每个父代码独立适应。

evidence.quote: These directives are then passed to the evolution module to generate framework-level patches. Finally, the updated agent is evaluated on downstream programming tasks via the action module. Agents that compile successfully and exhibit basic coding functionality are retained and added to the archive for future evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: 非权重框架patch的执行—保留—再进化闭环；不要求每孩子优于父亲。

evidence.quote: Finally, the top-2 performing agents from this stage are evaluated on the full SWE-bench Verified dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: 10任务sanity、50 Verified-Mini选优，再top2全量；Mini属全量子集，非完全密封留出。

evidence.quote: Agents achieving a success rate above 40% are subsequently evaluated on a separate, unseen 50-task medium set, ensuring that the larger set remains a strict out-of-distribution test for generalization.
evidence.support_explanation: 明确10任务进化/50任务分离作者声明；未说明多候选medium分数能否返用于选最终agent。

evidence.quote: To ensure fair comparison, we intentionally run the baseline for twice as many iterations as GEA so that the total number of evolved agents is comparable across methods, ensuring all comparisons are conducted under matched model schedules.
evidence.support_explanation: 匹配孩子数和Haiku/Sonnet切换日程，但非实测token/美元硬预算。

evidence.quote: On SWE-bench Verified, GEA improves performance from 20.0% to 71.0%, while under the same number of evolved agents, the DGM baseline achieves only 56.7%. On Polyglot, GEA boosts performance from 38.2% to 88.3%, significantly outperforming the DGM baseline (68.3%).
evidence.support_explanation: 主结果为作者报告，未复现；最终分母/跨run聚合不清，50例pass@1与88.3%等非整步数需说明。

evidence.quote: five of its integrated tools originated from different parent agents, confirming that explicit experience sharing prevents beneficial innovations from dying out.
evidence.support_explanation: 来源分析支持跨支系继承，不能单凭祖先数证明独立因果效应。

evidence.quote: Specifically, we replace the coding model used in the acting module with different GPT-series and Claude-series models during benchmark evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: 固定最佳框架换执行模型比较初始框架，支持非权重改进；图内逐模型数字无页图不可编造。

evidence.quote: We report the number of evolution iterations required to repair injected bugs across five independent trials (E1–E5).
evidence.support_explanation: 五次局部扰动试验给出每次修复轮数，不是整个搜索的五个独立种子。

evidence.quote: We then form a group consisting of this faulty agent and another bug-free agent from its original parent group, and perform group evolution to assess whether GEA can leverage experience from the better-performing agent (i.e., the one without framework-level bugs) to repair the faulty one.
evidence.support_explanation: GEA额外有健康同伴；因果结论为共享健康经验的恢复，不是无此帮助等信息预算算法优越性。

evidence.quote: the estimated cost of completing a full run is approximately USD 13,000 per method on SWE-bench and USD 1,500 on Polyglot.
evidence.support_explanation: 有全run成本估计，明细主要benchmark calls，不是每臂实测token/美元分布或固定预算。

evidence.quote: Updated tests logic
evidence.support_explanation: patch类型列出测试逻辑修改；缺具体diff，不能认定篡改评分器，也不能认为评测器不可改已审计。

evidence.support_explanation: 沙盒作者声明；编辑权限/评分器保护与回滚的细粒度边界未说明。

evidence.quote: GEA overcomes the limitation of inefficient utilization of exploratory diversity caused by isolated evolutionary branches
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: branch isolation in tree-structured open-ended evolution wastes exploratory diversity.

evidence.quote: although such systems often exhibit substantial exploratory diversity, this diversity rarely serves as effective stepping stones
evidence.support_explanation: Stated residual: diversity does not compound; cited to prior open-endedness literature, tested here through Fig 4 (tool propagation) and Table 1 (ancestor counts).

evidence.quote: GEA maintains an archive that stores all discovered agents throughout the evolutionary process.
evidence.support_explanation: Archive of agents is the persistent store; parents are selected from it each iteration.

evidence.quote: Performance serves as the primary selection criterion, while novelty is incorporated as a mild bias without dominating performance, enabling a balanced trade-off between exploitation and exploration.
evidence.support_explanation: Parent score = alpha_i x sqrt(nov(i)), top-K agents become the parent group.

evidence.quote: where each dimension indicates whether the agent successfully solves a corresponding probe task
evidence.support_explanation: Novelty uses a binary task-success vector; the probe task set (dimension D) and its relation to the evolution/test sets are not specified.

evidence.quote: denotes the performance of agent i i on downstream coding tasks
evidence.support_explanation: alpha_i is performance 'on downstream coding tasks' without naming the set; selection data therefore cannot be separated from reporting data.

evidence.quote: for a randomly sampled unsolved task during evaluation
evidence.support_explanation: Evolutionary traces include a predicted patch for an unsolved task of the benchmark plus logs and the evaluation outcome of that task, so benchmark tasks and their outcomes feed back into the improver.

evidence.quote: The aggregated traces from all agents in the parent group are provided as shared input to every agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Core operation: pooled patches, predicted task patches, execution logs and outcomes of all parents condition every member's reflection.

evidence.quote: Agents that compile successfully and exhibit basic coding functionality are retained and added to the archive for future evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Archive admission gate is only 'compiles and basic functionality' (staged sanity check of 10 tasks); no performance gate, regression test or rollback.

evidence.quote: The reflection module is consistently powered by GPT-o1
evidence.support_explanation: Reflection (trace analysis producing evolution directives) is a fixed external model distinct from the Claude acting/evolving model: part of the improver is outsourced and held constant.

evidence.quote: which is designed to preserve a similar difficulty and pass-rate distribution as the full benchmark with fewer samples
evidence.support_explanation: Selection uses a 50-task Verified-Mini (a small subset in the same benchmark family as the reporting set) after a 10-task sanity check; per-agent scores are therefore on about 60 tasks (cost table also lists 60 tasks).

evidence.quote: Finally, the top-2 performing agents from this stage are evaluated on the full SWE-bench Verified dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Only top-2 agents get a full-benchmark run, yet the headline comparison appears to use the staged numbers (Table 1 values 56.7/48.3/45.0/63.3/58.3 are all multiples of 1/60).

evidence.quote: group-level evolution is conducted exclusively on a 10-task small set. Agents achieving a success rate above 40% are subsequently evaluated on a separate, unseen 50-task medium set, ensuring that the larger set remains a strict out-of-distribution test for generalization.
evidence.support_explanation: Polyglot design separates a 10-task evolution set from a 50-task unseen set, but best-agent picking uses the unseen-set scores and the 88.3% equals 53/60, i.e. it looks like a pooled 60-task figure.

evidence.quote: to discard those with framework-level failures (i.e., cannot compile or solve 0 out of 10 tasks)
evidence.support_explanation: Sanity gate definition for archive admission.

evidence.quote: we set the group size to K = 2 K=2 and use M = 4 M=4 nearest neighbors in the KNN-based parent group selection.
evidence.support_explanation: Group size is 2 in all experiments; no group-size sweep.

evidence.quote: Due to computational budget constraints, during the first 20 iterations, the evolving and acting modules are powered by Claude Haiku 4.5
evidence.support_explanation: Acting/evolving model changes inside the run (SWE-bench: Haiku 4.5 for iterations 1-20, Sonnet 4.5 for 21-30; Polyglot 1-10 vs 11-20).

evidence.quote: while the final 10 iterations use Claude Sonnet 4.5
evidence.support_explanation: Late-run agents are scored with a stronger acting model than early ones, so archive scores used for parent ranking are not comparable across iterations and the reported rise from the iteration-0 score includes the model upgrade; only the transfer figure (Fig 5) controls the model.

evidence.quote: implemented following DGM
evidence.support_explanation: The baseline is the authors' re-implementation of DGM (single parent per iteration, one child, no sharing), not DGM's published run; parent-selection rule of the baseline is not described, so novelty-based selection and experience sharing are confounded.

evidence.quote: we intentionally run the baseline for twice as many iterations as GEA so that the total number of evolved agents is comparable across methods
evidence.support_explanation: Budget parity by number of evolved agents (60 each on SWE-bench) with matched Haiku-to-Sonnet schedules; reflection input size differs.

evidence.quote: On SWE-bench Verified, GEA improves performance from 20.0% to 71.0%, while under the same number of evolved agents, the DGM baseline achieves only 56.7%.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline; 20.0% = 12/60 and 56.7% = 34/60 imply 60-task denominators, while 71.0% is not a multiple of 1/60.

evidence.quote: On Polyglot, GEA boosts performance from 38.2% to 88.3%, significantly outperforming the DGM baseline (68.3%).
evidence.support_explanation: Polyglot headline: 88.3% = 53/60 and 68.3% = 41/60.

evidence.quote: GEA achieves performance comparable to or exceeding state-of-the-art human-designed agents on both benchmarks: 71.0% vs. 71.8% on SWE-bench Verified, and 88.3% vs. 52.0% on Polyglot.
evidence.support_explanation: Human-designed entries are full-benchmark leaderboard results with GPT-5 backbones (OpenHands, Aider); GEA numbers come from a 60-task staged evaluation with Claude models, so the comparison mixes subsets and backbones.
Worst-case success of the top-k and unique-ancestor counts: GEA's top-5 floor (58.3%) exceeds DGM's single best (56.7%); denominators are 60 (ancestor counts 17/60 = 28.3%); single run per method.

evidence.quote: GEA integrated eight of these functionalities into its best agent, whereas the best DGM agent integrated only five.
evidence.support_explanation: Observational evidence (nine tool-level modifications in Fig 4) that sharing propagates tools across branches in one GEA run versus one DGM run.

evidence.quote: Notably, GEA exhibits faster and more pronounced improvement in the mid-to-late stages of evolution compared to DGM
evidence.support_explanation: Mid-to-late stages coincide with the switch to Sonnet 4.5; claim of enhanced self-improvement ability is inferred from curves, not from a descendant-productivity measurement.

evidence.quote: GEA’s best-discovered agent driven by GPT-series and Claude-series models consistently achieve higher performance than their corresponding initial agents on both SWE-bench and Polyglot benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Model-transfer control against the iteration-0 agent per backbone; effect sizes are only in Fig 5 (not readable), and tasks are the same benchmark.
Iterations to repair an injected framework bug in five trials; per-trial values reported.

evidence.quote: For comparison, under the self-evolution setting, the bugged agent evolves independently without access to external experience sharing.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline has no access to a bug-free agent's traces while GEA's group contains one: the experiment tests information access by construction and does not control for it (a DGM variant allowed to read a better agent's traces is absent).

evidence.quote: the estimated cost of completing a full run is approximately USD 13,000 per method on SWE-bench and USD 1,500 on Polyglot
evidence.support_explanation: Cost estimate with per-model per-task breakdown; dominated by benchmark evaluation.

evidence.quote: Since we generate the same number of agents for both methods, their overall costs are very similar.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost parity argued from equal agent counts; extra reflection tokens from pooled traces and the o1 reflection spend are not itemised.

evidence.quote: docutils_debug +0.10 Modified core agent logic +0.10 Updated tests logic +0.22 Add snippet_extract tool +0.10
evidence.support_explanation: Top-1 lineage: the three largest gains (+0.10, +0.10, +0.22) come from a debugging patch, core-logic and test-running changes; deltas for the whole lineage sum to about +0.60 although the reported rise is 0.20 to 0.71, so deltas are not additive or are measured under different models.

evidence.quote: Across all three agents, the performance-improving patches primarily focus on enhancing the agents’ workflows and tool usage, rather than relying on model-specific prompting strategies.
evidence.support_explanation: Classification of patches by description is the evidence for model-agnostic gains.

evidence.quote: reaching 88.3% in just 4 iterations with a total of 8,677 lines of code added
evidence.support_explanation: Several thousand lines of added code per run; no audit of benchmark-specific content.

evidence.quote: the evolutionary process may inadvertently introduce directions misaligned with human intent while consuming substantial computational resources
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge cost/alignment risks; sandboxed experiments.

evidence.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.5 SWE-bench 60 $370
evidence.support_explanation: The breakdown covers only coding-model calls per 60 tasks. The o1 reflection calls and the larger pooled-trace inputs, which are exactly what GEA changes, are not itemised, and the totals are 'estimated'.

evidence.quote: To mitigate the substantial cost of evaluating every evolved agent on the full benchmarks, we adopt a staged evaluation strategy where agents must pass smaller subsets before advancing.
evidence.support_explanation: Per-agent scores come from staged subsets (10 + 50 tasks). The 1/60 granularity of 20.0/56.7/48.3/45.0/63.3/58.3 and of Polyglot 88.3/68.3 fits a 60-task pool, while the headline 71.0% does not.

signatures.output: Parent group G of size K

signatures.persistence: Archive is append-only for qualifying agents

gap.author_gap: Open-ended self-evolving agents evolve individual lineages in strictly isolated tree branches, so early exploratory discoveries are rarely consolidated into the best agent.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and partly measured in the paper: four of nine key tools found in isolated DGM branches never reached its best agent (Fig 4, in text), and ancestors per best agent are 9 vs 17. The causal role of isolation versus selection rule or sample count is not separated.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Ancestors: DGM (open-ended archive, the re-implemented baseline), quality-diversity novelty search (Mouret and Clune, Pugh et al., cited for the selection rule), reflection-based and chain-based self-improvers. Other population methods that already share information across candidates (cross-over, shared program database, group reflections) are not discussed or compared in the package text; neighbour originals absent.
gap.residue: Whether cross-lineage experience sharing, rather than larger parent group or novelty selection, drives consolidation; whether benefits persist beyond a single run and beyond K=2.
gap.stakes: Cumulative progress of self-modifying coding agents under a fixed evaluation budget (about USD 13,000 per run).
gap.method_response: Pool traces of a performance-novelty-selected parent group and let each member reflect on all of them.
gap.remaining_gap: Ablation of sharing vs selection, variance across runs, held-out evaluation of the best agent, and improver-level evidence.
unresolved: Closest alternatives' originals not in package
Whether DGM baseline uses its original selection rule

rs_pattern.reason: Opus follows sol and the run precedent r07b Huxley-Gödel Machine (a DGM-family modification → assumption_audit_and_pivot with H20). The audited, load-bearing assumption is single-parent lineage isolation. GEA violates it by pooling traces across a parent group and demonstrates the new behaviour (cross-branch tool consolidation). son55's generative_process_redesign is not retained: the 'fixed component' would be the evolutionary unit of a search procedure, which would make every change to an optimizer a liberated component (precedent r09b RoboPhD). No sub-card fits (C01/C05/C11/C19/C28/C29 concern safety, identifiability or bounds).

claims.text: GEA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art self-evolving methods under the same number of evolved agents.
claims.setting: SWE-bench Verified (about 60 tasks per agent in staging) and Polyglot (10 + 50 tasks), K=2, Claude Haiku/Sonnet 4.5 with GPT-o1 reflection
claims.baseline_control: Re-implemented DGM with 2x iterations (60 agents each)
claims.selection_vs_test: Same staged sets drive parent selection and reporting; only top-2 get a full-benchmark run; Polyglot has a 10-task evolution set and a 50-task unseen set whose scores are used to pick agents
claims.result_denominator: SWE 71.0% vs 56.7%; Polyglot 88.3% vs 68.3%; single run each; 1 task = 1.7 points
claims.allowed_conclusion: In one run per method on staged benchmark subsets, the group-sharing system reached higher scores than a DGM re-implementation at equal agent count; effect size and attribution to sharing are uncertain.

claims.text: GEA converts exploratory diversity into sustained progress by consolidating tools across branches.
claims.setting: Fig 4 tool-level analysis, Table 1 ancestor counts
claims.result_denominator: 8 of 9 tools integrated vs 5; 17 vs 9 ancestors
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptively, more discovered tools reach GEA's best agent in this run; no ablation shows sharing is the cause.

claims.text: GEA matches or exceeds top human-designed agent frameworks without human intervention.
claims.setting: Comparison with OpenHands + GPT-5 (71.8%) and Aider + GPT-5 (52.0%)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not supported as stated: the comparison mixes evaluation subsets and model backbones.

claims.text: Improvements transfer across coding models and are more robust to framework bugs.
claims.baseline_control: iteration-0 agent per backbone; independently evolving DGM agent
claims.result_denominator: bug repair 1.4 vs 5.0 iterations over 5 trials
claims.allowed_conclusion: Best agent beats its initial agent under several backbones (effect sizes unreadable); faster repair is expected from the added information access.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In a single evolution run per method with equal numbers of evolved agents, a group-pooled-experience evolver reached higher staged-benchmark scores and integrated more distinct tools into its best agent than a re-implemented DGM; transfer of the best agent across several coding backbones is reported against the initial agent.
unresolved: Contribution of experience sharing vs novelty selection vs K

assessment.level_reason: Opus sides with son55 (EVIDENCE rule 2; precedent r03b SICA). The comparative numbers are on the staged sets that drive parent selection, and the best Polyglot agent is picked by its medium-set score. Only the top-2 SWE agents get a full-benchmark run, and its denominator is ambiguous. Model transfer re-runs the same benchmark tasks. Retained code is reused across iterations, but no independent task set shows the retained edits help → task. Contrast r07b HGM (retained via 207 overlap-filtered Lite tasks).

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. A concrete bottleneck (isolated branches lose discovered tools), partly measured (4 of 9 tools never reach DGM's best agent), with DGM as the clear nearest neighbour. Not 4: population methods that already share information across candidates are not examined.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Pooling patches, logs and outcomes of a performance–novelty parent group into every member's reflection is a clear operation that predicts faster cross-branch propagation. Not 4: selection rule, K and extra context are not separated from sharing.

X.reason: Opus sides with son55. Algorithms 1–2 give the loop, but key conditions are unclear. The probe-task set behind z_i and the task set behind α_i are never named, and α mixes Haiku-era and Sonnet-era scores. Admission is compile/basic-function only, with no regression check or rollback. The reflection/evolution prompts are not given, and edit permissions are unaudited ('Updated tests logic'). This fits anchor 2 (key conditions and recovery unclear), unlike r07b HGM, whose algorithm and parameters were fully specified.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Execution-based pass rates are valid verifiers, but the headline figures mix denominators (1/60 multiples vs 71.0%, opus:O02), and the human-framework comparison sets 60-task Claude subsets against full-benchmark GPT-5 entries.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. There is one re-implemented DGM baseline at a matched agent count and model schedule, a backbone-transfer control and observational tool-provenance data. There is no ablation separating sharing from selection or K. The bug-repair test gives the treatment a healthy peer by construction.

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with son55 (precedent r03b SICA / cal-h1-v2 POET: selection and test coincide → 1). Staged sets drive both selection and reporting. Benchmark tasks and their outcomes feed the improver. The Polyglot '50-task unseen' set is used to pick agents, and 88.3% = 53/60 looks pooled with the 10 evolution tasks. Only the top-2 SWE agents get a full run (mostly unseen tasks, but its figure is ambiguous). sol's 2 took the Polyglot separation at face value.

E.statistics.reason: Opus sides with son55 (A2 ladder). The main result is one evolution run per method with no interval (one task = 1.7 points). The five bug-repair trials give per-trial counts for a secondary claim only, so the ladder's level 2 (uncertainty on the tested result) is not reached for the central claim.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol (precedent r07b HGM: totals without per-arm measured use → 2). Run totals (≈$13k SWE, ≈$1.5k Polyglot) and a per-60-task coding-model table are given. They are estimates, parity is argued from equal agent counts, and the o1 reflection calls and the larger pooled-trace inputs (the component GEA changes) are not itemised (opus:O01).
